policies.statement: Inside the catalog repository, the implementation generator is told to read components from the hand-built cartoon-chunky preview-place to absorb its register before generating; later guidance names four preview-place components as worked examples to imitate.
canExplainPatterns: preview-place-like module boundaries
shared component implementation shapes
shared naming and code register even across unrelated tastes

policies.statement: DESIGN.roblox.md sections that are present must use one canonical order, with duplicate canonical sections rejected and unknown sections preserved.
canExplainPatterns: the same section sequence across extracted tastes
the same eleven-section document skeleton
identical placement of Roblox extension sections

policies.statement: Extraction should use the configured recommended token names whenever they fit and invent names only when the recommendations do not cover the concept, explicitly to make runs near-deterministic.
canExplainPatterns: shared color keys such as primary, surface, outline, and currency-soft
shared typography tiers display, heading, body, label, and caption
shared spacing and rounded token ladders

policies.statement: Colors are assigned to prescribed semantic roles by behavior rather than hue, including primary, danger, surface roles, currency roles, rarity accent, outline, and dim.
canExplainPatterns: the same semantic palette role names across independent tastes
dominant forward actions consistently becoming primary
close or destructive controls consistently becoming danger

policies.statement: Observed lettering is mapped to the nearest family in a normative Roblox font-family table; Gotham and Arial families must never be emitted because the engine removed and remaps them.
canExplainPatterns: repeated FredokaOne for rounded cartoon lettering
repeated Montserrat or BuilderSans for neutral lettering
repeated Oswald for condensed heavy lettering
absence of Gotham and Arial in generated code

policies.statement: Measured geometry is rounded to friendly steps: spacing to 4px, radii to 2px, and strokes to 1px.
canExplainPatterns: geometry concentrated on common integer steps
recurring multiples of four in spacing
recurring even-number radii
integer stroke widths

policies.statement: Observed typography sizes are normalized into five named tiers—display, heading, body, label, and caption—and unobserved tiers are skipped.
canExplainPatterns: the same typography tier taxonomy across tastes
consistent omission of unobserved tiers
similar bindings between headings, buttons, body copy, and captions

policies.statement: Every still-image extraction ships one of four taste-family motion preset blocks; video may override values only through bucket classification, and motion must not be claimed as observed without video.
canExplainPatterns: identical duration ladders within taste-family classifications
shared easing combinations such as Back Out plus Quad Out/In
common overshoot, fade, slide, or no-bounce prose within a family
low Motion confidence when no video exists

policies.statement: Every ornament must be classified as either a Roblox UI primitive or a pre-rendered image asset; differing-per-item visuals, baked type, 3D shading, and light bursts are treated as asset slots rather than primitive recipes.
canExplainPatterns: shared ImageLabel boundaries for wordmarks, faceted items, and burst art
shared UIGradient/UIStroke/UICorner treatment for primitive fills and outlines
similar avoidance of reconstructed baked art

policies.statement: Generation starts with Theme.luau as a mechanical front-matter translation; component visuals bind to Theme, token names become camelCase fields, and literal visual constants outside Theme are defects except for values inlined by the DESIGN document.
canExplainPatterns: a Theme.luau in every implementation
the same token-to-Luau table shapes
camelCase Theme field names
absence of literal colors and durations in components

policies.statement: When a needed visual value lacks a front-matter token but the taste gives a basis, it is derived in Theme and marked Derived; prescribed examples include sky-like backdrops for bright tastes, moody backdrops for dark tastes, pressed lifts, and dim washes.
canExplainPatterns: shared Theme.derived tables
sky-like versus moody story backdrops
computed pressed colors and dim overlays centralized in Theme
complete derived rarity bevel sets

policies.statement: The output uses a prescribed src tree with Theme, Components, Screens, Stories, and a storybook module; screens may compose themed components but may not draw styled repeating shapes inline.
canExplainPatterns: identical directory trees
one component module per DESIGN component
separate screen and story modules
promotion of repeated styled rows and cells into components

policies.statement: The component procedure presents two worked archetypes: a beveled root/Face structure whose bevel collapses when pressed, and a flat/translucent single-frame structure whose pressed feedback is a brightness or stroke lift.
canExplainPatterns: root plus Face layering in chunky implementations
single-frame translucent panels in dark implementations
bevel collapse or brightness-lift press states

policies.statement: Generated components implement pressed, disabled, and selected states through prescribed props/events and expose standard size, position, anchorPoint, layoutOrder, zIndex, and activation passthroughs.
canExplainPatterns: matching prop names across unrelated components
useState-driven MouseButton1Down/Up/Leave handling
selected and disabled props on many modules
variant maps at module scope

policies.statement: Repeating content must use UIListLayout or UIGridLayout, containers and screens are Scale-first with UIAspectRatioConstraint, and button/header text uses TextScaled plus UITextSizeConstraint while body/caption text uses fixed TextSize.
canExplainPatterns: shared UIListLayout and UIGridLayout trees
shared Scale-based container sizing
UIAspectRatioConstraint on scale-driven elements
TextScaled headers and buttons but fixed-size body text

policies.statement: Every generated ScreenGui explicitly sets ZIndexBehavior to Sibling because Global is the engine default and can hide default-ZIndex descendants under overlays.
canExplainPatterns: ZIndexBehavior.Sibling in every ScreenGui
sibling shadow and panel layering
avoidance of child shadows behind parent panels

policies.statement: With Sibling behavior, generated ScreenGuis reserve DisplayOrder bands of HUD 0–9, windows 10–19, popups/toasts 20–29, and tooltips 30+, reproducing the bands with sibling ZIndex inside a single ScreenGui.
canExplainPatterns: the same cross-screen layer bands
windows consistently above HUD
popups and tooltips consistently above windows

policies.statement: Any content-bearing window must use a Scale-first panel around 0.85 by 0.85 with a desktop MaxSize, keep header and close controls on-screen, and use a ScrollingFrame when content can overflow; delivery must also verify desktop and 667×375 landscape.
canExplainPatterns: similar 0.85-scale window roots
UISizeConstraint desktop caps
scrolling shop/list content
667×375 responsive accommodations

policies.statement: Every interactive element has a minimum 44px logical touch target; a smaller visual token stays at its taste size inside an invisible 44px-or-larger interactive root, while chunky tastes prefer 56px or more.
canExplainPatterns: invisible enlarged hit roots around price pills
44px minimum close and icon buttons
56px-or-larger chunky controls

policies.statement: HUDs keep the joystick, jump-button, and topbar zones clear, and hover-only affordances require a touch-visible equivalent.
canExplainPatterns: empty bottom-left and bottom-right HUD zones
top-offset HUD clusters
touch-visible alternatives to hover

policies.statement: When a DESIGN document defines press squash, the implementation pattern is UIScale plus a ref plus TweenService; animatable values derive from Theme.motion and task.wait is forbidden for animation timing.
canExplainPatterns: UIScale children on buttons and windows
TweenService-created press and entrance tweens
Theme.motion duration and easing lookups
MouseLeave restoring press scale

policies.statement: Worked motion snippets use a 0.92 press target and describe a 0.8-to-1.0 entrance pop as an example; those numbers are examples, not unconditional requirements.
canExplainPatterns: repeated 0.92 press squash values
repeated 0.8 entrance start scales
similar press-in and press-out tween wiring

policies.statement: Catalog/e2e slices implement the same fixed showcase: the minimum component slots and exactly HUD.story, Shop.story, and Dialog.story with prescribed labels, counts, six ordered items, rarity roles, prices, and dialog copy.
canExplainPatterns: identical story names
12,400 soft currency and 99 hard currency
SHOP, ITEMS, SETTINGS, and PLAY labels
Acorn, Feather, Crystal, Lantern, Compass, and Crown in the same order
shared confirm-dialog copy

policies.statement: Standard Showcase implementations check and reuse an arbitrated canonical asset table first, after a taste-specific pixel check; fresh searches are the exception.
canExplainPatterns: the same icon and item image IDs across tastes
shared Acorn, Feather, Crystal, Lantern, Compass, and Crown artwork
shared white tintable shop, item, settings, and currency icons

policies.statement: Every component and screen gets a UI-Labs story, stories use the prescribed React story shape and a world-like backdrop, and available verification proceeds through syntax, visual capture, numeric state/motion assertions, and a fixed rubric.
canExplainPatterns: matching story module shapes
world-like story backdrops
controls for text, counts, disabled state, and progress
the same 3-second wayfinding, CTA, tap-target, contrast, and token-fidelity checks

policies.statement: Extraction records an input and element for every token, marks default-affected sections low confidence, states defaults inline, and never presents a default as observed.
canExplainPatterns: similar extraction provenance blocks
low Motion confidence without video
explicit notes for omitted or defaulted sections
consistent omission of unseen components and states

policies.statement: Generation uses the React 17 Luau API surface and must not emit JSX, Roact APIs, Suspense/lazy/error boundaries, camelCase event props, legacy Font assignments, JavaScript ternaries, or JavaScript destructuring.
canExplainPatterns: React.createElement calls instead of JSX
ReactRoblox.createRoot mounting
bracketed React.Event handlers
FontFace assignments
Luau if-expressions and multiple returns

knownValidationGaps.gap: The bundled linter fails the process only for error-severity findings. Section order, CSS vocabulary, unknown component properties, and missing primary are warnings; missing extraction confidence is only info. Therefore a zero-error result does not validate canonical order, warning-free prose, provenance completeness, visual fidelity, interaction behavior, or source-taste accuracy.
Visual QA is conditional on a connected Roblox Studio MCP, and multi-resolution review is conditional on emulation availability; syntax checking remains the only always-available layer.
The reported Phase 4 pass did not perform multi-resolution validation, and the report records MCP device-emulation operation as unverified.
Motion video overrides had no end-to-end or field example in the calibration and Phase 4 reports.
Touch-independent tooltip or hover fallback guidance was recorded as prose-only rather than validated implementation behavior.
Catalog preview persistence was not validated; Phase 4 says screen_capture existed only in context and required a manual screenshot or a capture-rig variant for site publication.
Calibration still found selected-versus-rarity interpretation ambiguous and missed a faint window shadow in one blind run.

The passing Phase 4 implementation is reported as having two stories, while the current Standard Showcase requires exactly three; that report does not establish conformance to the current fixed showcase contract.

The top-level skill says catalog icon and texture slots get real image assets rather than glyph placeholders, but the asset reference permits a procedural or glyph placeholder after an honest unsuccessful search; the mandatory surface and its fallback are not stated consistently.

The first round-trip calibration was explicitly highly contaminated because the extractor session knew the golden answers; the blind runs found a rendering bug and a wrong measurement rule that the contaminated run did not catch.

independenceRisks: The implementation skill explicitly routes catalog generators through the same cartoon-chunky preview-place register and named worked components; shared component anatomy or code shape may reflect that seed rather than independent source tastes (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/SKILL.md:10-15; skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/generation-procedure.md:118-121).

The Standard Showcase intentionally fixes story names, labels, currency counts, item identities/order, prices, dialog copy, and minimum component slots. Those corpus similarities are controlled comparison content, not evidence that the source tastes independently share them (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/standard-showcase.md:1-99).

The canonical asset registry intentionally reuses the same image IDs across tastes. Common icon/item artwork and associated aspect or transparency handling are generator contamination, not independent taste observations (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/asset-sourcing.md:78-122).

Canonical section order, recommended token names, five typography tiers, semantic color roles, and geometry quantization deliberately reduce extraction variance. Their recurrence across DESIGN documents cannot by itself support a claim of taste similarity (skills/screenshot-to-designmd/SKILL.md:56-62; skills/screenshot-to-designmd/references/extraction-procedure.md:43-45,89-117).

The four family-level motion presets inject durations, easings, and prose when no video exists. Shared motion among tastes assigned to the same family may be wholly defaulted rather than observed (skills/screenshot-to-designmd/references/motion-presets.md:1-59).

The 44px/56px touch-target rule, reserved HUD zones, Scale-first layout, Sibling ZIndex behavior, layer bands, and the 667×375 viewport requirement impose common interaction and layout geometry independently of the screenshots (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/layout-rules.md:19-56,86-114).

Both skills carry generated copies of the same root spec/config, so extraction and implementation are coupled through one schema rather than independent stages; a convention in the shared spec propagates to both sides of the round trip (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/spec/spec-config.yaml:1-23; skills/screenshot-to-designmd/references/spec/spec-config.yaml:1-23).

The calibration report says section structure, token naming, component anatomy, and omission patterns were identical across all three runs because of vocabulary constraints. That is direct evidence of policy-driven convergence, including on anatomy, even when two runs were blind (skills/screenshot-to-designmd/calibration/2026-07-12-round-trip/report.md:46-57).

Fourteen skill/spec changes were folded back from one Phase 4 opposite-taste run, including two press archetypes, brightness/stroke lifts, CanvasGroup guidance, invisible touch roots, safe glyphs, and ZIndex bands. Later e2e implementations can converge on those case-derived remedies even when their tastes are independent (docs/phase4-e2e-report.md:40-50).

The Phase 4 input set came from one named horror title and included community-Wiki material; its successful two-story implementation then informed general generator policy. This is a narrow empirical base for conventions applied corpus-wide (docs/phase4-e2e-report.md:8-18,29-31,40-50).

The shared verification rubric can select for the same visible outcomes—persistent CTA/currency, enlarged hit areas, contrast treatment, and multi-resolution containment—regardless of whether those outcomes were visible in the original screenshots (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/verification.md:115-123).

Worked numeric motion examples such as 0.92 press squash and 0.8 entrance scale can become copied constants even though the document presents them as examples rather than universal requirements (skills/designmd-to-react-lua/references/motion-implementation.md:10-29,42-64).
